title: Hermes: an all-in-one entropy tool
description:
Hermes computes the entropy of a phase term by term from atomistic simulation and turns it into CALPHAD input.

The vibrational entropy of a crystal comes from molecular dynamics positions, either by compression (a clean-room implementation written from the preprint of Fisher and Hong, arXiv:2512.02221) or from the Gaussian covariance of the displacements, less the entropy the atoms share. Near melting it is carried up from about a third of the melting point by the heat capacity of NPT runs. Further terms: the quantum correction from the MD velocity spectrum, liquid entropy from partial pair distribution functions, excess mixing entropy from composition fluctuations, and configurational entropy over listed configurations through the zentropy core of pyzentropy 0.1.1 (N. L. E. Hew, Phases Research Lab, MIT license).

New in 0.2.0 are three terms that atomic motion does not carry. The crystal-field entropy of lanthanide ions comes from measured level energies. Magnetic entropy and Gibbs energy follow the Inden / Hillert-Jarl model, with an explicit choice of reference so that the ordering energy already in a 0 K calculation is not counted twice. Electronic entropy comes from a density of states. These three are so far checked against exact results only; a test against measured entropies has been pre-registered and not yet run.

Output: Redlich-Kister parameters as TDB lines for pycalphad, and mixing and formation data (enthalpy, entropy, heat capacity) as ESPEI datasets. The solid and mixing routes are checked against thermodynamic integration in tests whose pass rules were fixed before the runs; every result, failures included, is in docs/validation.md.
